title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page). S is a normal integral scheme of finite type over a prime field, say Q, of dimension N. K is its function field. X -> S is a relative smooth compactification of a family U -> S of hyperbolic curves. E_K = pi_1(U_K) is the arithmetic fundamental group of the generic fibre, an extension of Gal(Kbar/K) by the geometric group pi. A section xi of E_{U_K} -> E_K is given, coming from a rational point of U_K, i.e. a rational section f of U over S.

The page localises at a codimension-1 point s of S, with residue field k(s) of transcendence degree N-1. S~ is the strict henselisation (a DVR), U~ is the induced family over it, and s' is a point above s in the normalisation of S in Kbar. The decomposition group N_{s'} (written E_U~) sits in an extension 1 -> I_{s'} -> N_{s'} -> E_{k(s)} -> 1, with inertia I_{s'} isomorphic to T = Zhat'(1).

Previous page. These conditions are equivalent:
- the composite I_{s'} -> pi is injective;
- the restriction of xi to N_{s'} does not come from a section of E_{U_s} over E_{k(s)};
- f is not regular at s, i.e. f(s) is a cusp i in X_s \ U_s.
In that case I_{s'} -> pi is k_i composed with multiplication by mu. Here k_i is the inclusion of the cusp inertia L_i = T, and mu >= 1 is the order of contact of f with the cusp divisor. So N_{s'} becomes a subgroup of index mu in the normaliser N(L_i), i.e. the decomposition group of the cusp i.

This page. Although the section of E_K over E_S does not extend over E_O~, it still defines a lift of the subgroup N_{s'}. Only the factor I_{s'} = T obstructs a genuine lift. N_{s'} embeds in N_{E_{X_s}}(L_i). Hence every splitting of the extension 1 -> T -> N_{s'} -> E_{k(s)} -> 1 yields a section of E_{X_s} over E_{k(s)}. This is the section attached to the rational point f(s) of the compactified fibre X_s, i.e. a 'cuspidal' or 'packet' section. It comes with extra data (the illegible underlined word, perhaps tangential or 'derivation' data, plus the multiplicity mu).

Second formulation, begun here and developed on the next page. A rational section f of U/S with domain the open S' is read as the family of points f(s) in U_s for s in S'. In group terms, a section of E_{U_K} over E_K gives a family of sections of E_{X_s} over E_{k(s)}, for all points s of S' and not only codimension 1. This uses the stabilisers N_{s'} in E_K of points s' of the normalisation of S in Kbar, whose inertia is no longer just T.

Purpose: the specialisation behaviour of the section conjecture. It aims at comparing sections over function fields of transcendence degree N with sections over residue fields of degree N-1, an inductive mechanism for the section conjecture over fields of finite type over Q.
errors: The text writes N_{E_{X_s}}(L_i), but L_i (the cusp inertia) lives in E_{U_s}. Presumably the normaliser of L_i in E_{U_s} is meant, followed by mapping to E_{X_s}. This is sloppy notation rather than a mathematical error.

'Every section of the extension gives a section of E_{X_s} over E_{k(s)}' needs the remark that the image is independent of the splitting up to conjugacy. The resulting section is just the one of the rational point f(s) of X_s, so the extra splitting data is not seen in X_s. Grothendieck hints at this with 'mais de ... en plus' but does not spell it out.
The splitting of 1 -> T -> N_{s'} -> E_{k(s)} -> 1 can be obstructed in general. Its existence here is guaranteed by the fact that the section xi exists; this is implicit, not stated.

ideas.what: Restriction of a section of the generic fibre's arithmetic fundamental group to a decomposition group at a codimension-1 point. It extends to a section over the residue field iff the rational point specialises into U_s; otherwise inertia injects into a cusp inertia L_i with index mu.
ideas.modern_name: specialisation of sections / cuspidal sections; inertia-defined criterion for good reduction of a rational point
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura (cuspidal sections, tangential points), Stix (Rational points and arithmetic of fundamental groups, LNM 2054; specialisation of sections), Hoshi, Saïdi
ideas.where_published: Section conjecture in the letter to Faltings (1983); this local analysis is not, to my knowledge, in published Grothendieck texts

ideas.what: The decomposition group N_{s'} embeds with finite index mu (the order of contact) in the normaliser of the cusp inertia, the decomposition group of the cusp. Splittings of it yield 'sections at infinity' of the compactified fibre.
ideas.modern_name: packets of cuspidal sections / tangential base points at cusps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989), Nakamura, Esnault–Wittenberg, Stix

ideas.what: A rational section of U/S viewed as a family of sections of E_{X_s} over E_{k(s)} for all points s of the domain. Built via stabilisers in E_K of points of the normalisation of S in Kbar, with general (not cyclic) inertia.
ideas.modern_name: specialisation of Galois sections to all points; birational / function-field section conjecture by induction on transcendence degree

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins describing how one section over the generic point yields a coherent family of (possibly cuspidal) sections over all residue fields k(s), s in S'. This includes higher-codimension points, where inertia is a bigger group than T, plus extra data beyond the point f(s). The converse is not worked out: reconstructing a generic section from such compatible families, as a specialisation/induction route for the section conjecture over fields of finite type. Also not worked out is what the extra splitting data ('... en plus') encodes.
missed.quote: toute section de cette extension de E_{k(s)} par T donne donc une section de E_{X_s} sur E_{k(s)} — mais de dérivation [?] en plus
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The section conjecture over fields of finite type over Q is open. A clean dictionary between sections over K and compatible families of sections over all residue fields, including higher-codimension inertia and cuspidal packets, is only partially available (Stix, Esnault–Wittenberg). The splitting data beyond f(s) resembles tangential-base-point data.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early (c.1981) careful analysis of specialising a Galois section at a codimension-1 point. It includes the multiplicity-mu embedding into the cusp decomposition group and the cuspidal-section phenomenon. These are now known (Nakamura, Stix, Hoshi) but are not credited to Grothendieck in the literature; the page itself is fragmentary and the results are standard today.
transcription_corrections: 'ni [?] = de' reads 'ni de'; the deleted word before 'des sous-groupes' is likely 'sur', and the phrase may be 'définit néanmoins, sur le sous-groupe E_Ũ = N_{s'} de E_K'.
'un facteur trivial humainement [?]' is uncertain. The sense is 'extension d'un E_k par un facteur [cyclique] isomorphe à T ≃ I_{s'}'.
'sur un corps de nf [?]' is likely 'sur un corps premier, disons Q'.
'presque [?] mais relèvement' is likely 'presque un relèvement' (underlined 'presque').
In 'N_{E_{X_s}}(L_i)' the subscript is indeed E_{X_s} in the image, though E_{U_s} is presumably meant.
The underlined word before 'en plus' is uncertain ('dérivation'? 'données'?).
'section rationnelle de U_S [?]' is likely 'section rationnelle de U/S'.
'Une autre façon de dire ces choses est la suivante' is correct; the crossed-out 'Une' precedes it.
